entries.0577702a4106e40a: This business manufactures and sells chilled foods such as boxed meals and prepared dishes. Sales promotion effects at convenience stores were significant, and sales of boxed meals and prepared dishes remained strong following the previous year, resulting in higher revenue. Manufacturing facilities for chilled foods are located at the Isesaki, Yachiyo, Itami and Gunma plants of Nihon Derika Sabisu Co., Ltd. (as of March 31, 2026).
entries.1b78c59f4f7e83e8: This business catches fish, raises fish, and processes and sells them. It comprises three businesses: the Fishing Business, the Aquaculture Business, and the Processing and Trading Business. Consolidated subsidiaries include Kurose Suisan Co., Ltd. and NISSUI USA, INC., and affiliates include Daisui Co., Ltd., among others. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥380,151 million (up 4.4% year on year), the second largest after the Food Business.
entries.1e65b91d75bf0f66: This business stores frozen and refrigerated products. Cold storage facilities are located at the Kawasaki Logistics Center, Hakozaki Logistics Center and Osaka Maishima Logistics Center of Nissui Butsuryu Co., Ltd. (as of March 31, 2026).

entries.41718e4b0293ba89: This business processes and sells marine products. In Japan, the business recovered from the third quarter owing to increased sales volume of fish oil and the effect of price revisions for salmon and trout, but the effects of the first half remained, and for the full year revenue increased. In North America, the processing business increased the share of Alaska pollock fillet production, and selling prices for surimi also rose. In the trading business, sales of Pacific cod, salmon and trout, and crab were firm, and overall revenue increased. In Europe, sales in Italy, the Benelux countries and the United Kingdom were firm, and revenue increased.

entries.8504d7d7f195f9a2: This business operates cold storage warehouses and provides delivery and customs clearance services. Consolidated subsidiaries are three companies, including Nissui Butsuryu Co., Ltd., and there are two affiliates. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥16,615 million (up 0.5% year on year). In addition, intersegment revenue from other segments within the group (internal segment revenue or transfers) amounted to ¥14,215 million, roughly the same size as revenue from external customers.
entries.8732db1711840433: This business catches fish using vessels. In Japan, catches of yellowtail, horse mackerel and mackerel were strong, and selling prices also rose, resulting in higher revenue. In South America, one of its two vessels was withdrawn from service, so catch volume declined and revenue decreased.
entries.905995615982480d: This business manufactures and sells pharmaceutical ingredients, raw materials for dietary supplements, and health foods. The company and one consolidated subsidiary carry out this business. Functional ingredients are EPA, DHA and similar materials used as raw materials for supplements and as additives to infant formula. Functional foods are mainly foods with function claims sold by mail order, such as “Goma Tonyu Shitate no Minna no Mikata DHA,” and foods for specified health uses, such as “Imaku S.” Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥16,982 million (up 7.2% year on year), with sales of pharmaceutical ingredients and domestic sales of functional ingredients for supplements being firm.

entries.a1664e28477c962d: This business manufactures and sells frozen foods and processed fish paste products for household and business use. In Japan, household chikuwa and fish sausages performed well, and frozen foods for restaurant and mass retail prepared-food channels were also firm. In North America, household products were firm and expanded market share, while business-use products were affected by lower demand from restaurants and higher raw material prices due to U.S. tariffs; overall, revenue increased. In Europe, sales in France, the United Kingdom and Spain were strong, and revenue increased.

entries.c4bbb9b8ad56b4e9: This business raises and sells fish. In Japan, the share of short-term farmed bluefin tuna production increased, yellowtail selling prices rose, and coho salmon output was increased, resulting in higher revenue. In South America, sales volume of coho salmon increased, sales to North America were strengthened, the share of value-added products with a higher degree of processing rose, and selling prices also rose, resulting in higher revenue. PESQUERA YADRAN S.A., a Chilean salmon farming company, has become a consolidated subsidiary after SALMONES ANTARTICA S.A. acquired it in January 2026.

entries.db0ff93253b60b01: This business manufactures and sells frozen foods, marine paste products such as chikuwa and fish sausage, and chilled foods such as boxed lunches and side dishes. It consists of two businesses: the processed foods business and the chilled foods business. Consolidated subsidiaries include Nihon Delica Service Co., Ltd. and GORTON'S, INC., among others. Net sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥500,985 million (up 6.4% year on year), the largest business in the group. Frozen foods for households, frozen foods for restaurants and mass retailers, and boxed lunches and side dishes for convenience stores grew. The major customer is SCI Co., Ltd., and sales to this customer were ¥123,180 million, or 13.2% of consolidated net sales.
